newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end higher on Sammi trouble.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end higher on Sammi trouble.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed higher on Friday in thin trading as the Sammi Group's financial difficulties continued to depress sentiment, brokers said.
The closing level of 12,88 was the highest since September 19, 1995, when yields closed at 12.90 percent.
"Yields rose to a new 18-month high on worries over tightening liquidity," said a Daishin Securities broker.
"Smaller-than-expected new issues for April failed to boost buying," he said. New issues were estimated at 2.6 trillion won in April, compared with 3.1 trillion won in March.
Three-month CDs rose slightly as a result of the Sammi failure, but they said the overnight call rate began to fall as banks looked ready to meet the central bank's reserve requirements on Saturday..
